overview.en: The Netted Mountain Moth is listed here as Macaria carbonaria, but a 2024 molecular revision transferred it to Epelis carbonaria.
overview.fr: Le Netted Mountain Moth est répertorié ici sous le nom Macaria carbonaria, mais une révision moléculaire de 2024 l’a transféré dans le genre Epelis.

identification.en: It is a small geometrid moth; the British account gives a wingspan of about 23–25 mm.
identification.fr: C’est un petit papillon de nuit géométridé ; la fiche britannique indique une envergure d’environ 23 à 25 mm.

habitat.en: In Britain it is known from Scottish Highland moorland and mountain slopes, while European records also include heathland and raised bogs.
habitat.fr: En Grande-Bretagne, il est connu des landes et versants montagneux des Highlands écossais ; les données européennes incluent aussi des landes et des tourbières hautes.

diet.en: The caterpillars feed on bearberry; a Norwegian account also lists bog-rosemary as a host plant.
diet.fr: Les chenilles se nourrissent de busserole ; une fiche norvégienne cite aussi le romarin des marais comme plante hôte.

behavior.en: Adults fly by day in spring and early summer and visit flowers growing in the habitat.
behavior.fr: Les adultes volent le jour au printemps et au début de l’été et visitent les fleurs présentes dans leur milieu.

reproduction.en: The sources consulted identify its larval host plants but do not give a verified clutch size or brood count.
reproduction.fr: Les sources consultées indiquent ses plantes hôtes larvaires, mais ne donnent ni taille de ponte ni nombre de générations vérifiés.

ecology.en: Unlike the bilberry-feeding Rannoch Looper, now placed in Speranza, this species is associated with bearberry and other northern heath or bog plants.
ecology.fr: Contrairement au Rannoch Looper, désormais placé dans Speranza et dont les chenilles mangent la myrtille, cette espèce est associée à la busserole et à d’autres plantes nordiques des landes et tourbières.

conservation.en: A Scottish site review describes it as confined in Britain to the Highlands and notes low dispersal and vulnerability to habitat change; these are regional, historically based observations.
conservation.fr: Une étude écossaise de sites le décrit comme limité en Grande-Bretagne aux Highlands et signale sa faible capacité de dispersion et sa vulnérabilité aux changements d’habitat ; ces observations sont régionales et anciennes.

facts: British account: 23–25 mm wingspan, Scottish Highland moors and mountains, day-flying adults visiting flowers, and larvae feeding on bearberry.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

facts: Norwegian account gives a northern and central European range, peatland and heath habitat, and larval food plants including bog-rosemary and bearberry.

facts: The older Scottish report describes the British species as confined to the Highlands, with poor dispersal and threats including drainage and habitat succession.

facts: The European species account lists moorland, heathland and raised bogs and documents multilingual common names including the French Philobie enfumée.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

uncertainties: The illustrated-species inventory retains Macaria carbonaria; recent literature uses Epelis carbonaria, and that current combination is mentioned while the inventory name remains the profile key.
The Scottish dispersal and pressure information comes from an older, site-focused assessment and does not establish current status across the full range.
Larval host lists differ among regional sources; only bearberry is consistently supported by the British and Norwegian accounts.
review_note: Cross-checked UK, Norwegian and pan-European species resources plus the molecular revision; reciprocal comparison with the inventory entry for the former Macaria brunneata is included.
